_readme: All guidance text for the India build (sold on the Wiz Designs site, not on Etsy). Edit any text here; keep the keys.

layoutBlurbs.fresher: Final-year students and freshers with no full-time job yet
layoutBlurbs.serviceIT: Freshers applying to IT service companies and tech roles
layoutBlurbs.nonIT: Commerce, arts, science and other non-IT roles
layoutBlurbs.govt: Government, PSU and other jobs where the form asks for personal details
layoutBlurbs.careerBreak: Coming back to work after a gap

tips.personal: Use one phone number and an email that looks professional (your name, not a nickname). City is enough; skip your full home address.
tips.headline: One line that says what you are and what you're looking for. You can reuse it as your Naukri and LinkedIn headline.
tips.summary: 2–3 short lines: your degree or current role, your strongest skills, and the kind of job you want. Write it for this job, not for every job.
tips.education: Newest first. Add your CGPA, and your 12th and 10th marks if they're good or the job asks for them; many Indian job filters read these.
tips.skills: List only what you can talk about in an interview. Put the skills the job post asks for first.
tips.projects: Say what you built, what you used, and what it did. Start each bullet with an action word like Built, Designed or Tested.
tips.internships: Even a short or unpaid internship counts. Write what you worked on, not just the company name.
tips.experience: Newest first. 3–5 bullets each, about what you did and what changed because of it.
tips.certifications: Name, who gave it, and the year. Leave out ones that have nothing to do with this job.
tips.achievements: Ranks, prizes, scholarships, hackathons, sports or arts at college or state level.
tips.activities: Clubs, NSS/NCC, volunteering, college fests, or anything where you organised or led something.
tips.languages: List the languages you can speak or write, e.g. English, Malayalam, Hindi.
tips.courses: Courses or certificates you did during the break show you kept learning. Add the year.
tips.breakNote: One honest line is enough, e.g. 'Took a career break (2023–2025) for family reasons; now returning to full-time work.' No long explanations.

checklistNotes.onePage: For freshers, one page is enough. Recruiters skim; a second page usually doesn't get read.
checklistNotes.contact: Phone and email as plain text, so software and people can copy them. No icons.
checklistNotes.headings: Standard headings like Education, Skills and Projects are what software and recruiters look for.
checklistNotes.photo: Private companies don't need a photo. Government forms usually have their own photo field.
checklistNotes.bullets: 3–5 bullets per project or job is easy to read. One bullet looks thin; eight is too long.
checklistNotes.dates: Write all dates the same way, e.g. 'Jun 2024' everywhere.
checklistNotes.fileName: Name the file with your name, so it's easy to find in a recruiter's inbox.

howToUse: Tap New resume and pick the layout closest to your situation.
Fill in each section in Build. Tap See an example when you're stuck, then change it to your own words.
Before applying, open Tailor, paste the job post and see which of its words your resume doesn't use. Add only the ones that are true for you, and save a copy for that job.
Open Check and fix anything marked. Run the copy-paste test on your PDF.
Open Export, save the PDF and Word file, and back up your data from More once a week.
govtNote: Many government forms ask for these in their own fields; add them here only if the notice asks.
